newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 9.
newsitem.headline: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek
press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis receives the first blow. Ten
ruling party PASOK MPs stray from the fold and fail to vote for
the party's choice for parliament speaker. Second round of
voting brings some - but not all - back. Personal bitterness may
be the cause but the creation of a "leftwing opposition" within
the party itself is also a possibility. Today's voting for
parliament officials will show if yesterday's rebellion will
continue.
--'Routine' Turkish provocations in the Aegean results in
one F-16 down off Chios, one pilot safe but the other still
missing. Defence Minister Akis Tsohadzopoulos says peace not
promoted in this way.
--Labour Minister Evangelos Yiannopoulos denies he gave the
order to arrest three journalists at a private radio station
after it claimed he was one of the dissenting PASOK deputies.
--And main opposition New Democracy's woes are not over. ND's
candidate for speaker was not supported by all the party's MPs.
TA NEA
--The 'haves" will pay more taxes to support the economically
weaker, Simitis says. Finance ministry officials are setting up
three "traps" -exclusion from tax exemptions and breaks, wealth
indicators and mulitiple tax checks - to snare high-income
earners.
ETHNOS
--Employee perks at state utilities and organisations (DEKO) -
including cheaper electricity, phone and water rates and free
rail and air tickets - to go, but the government appears willing
to discuss replacing them with increases in wages to offset
industrial action.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--Ten dissenters in Parliament send a message of rebellion to
PASOK.
KATHIMERINI
--Fateful provocation: Ankara plays down the loss of its F-16
in the Aegean while violating Greek air space yesterday. US
urges Greece and Turkey to once again talk over differences in
the Aegean.
--Fuel throws a shadow over cost of living index - encouraging
downward trend in foodstuffs offset by continuing increase of
fuels, which may prove fatal to government optimism for
8.0 percent inflation at year's end.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou and 'Casino Rhodes'
consortium expected to sign contract within the next few days.
--Finance ministry imagination works overtime on how to draw
more tax revenues. Apart from the drastic cutback on tax
exemptions, the government is proceeding with the imposition of
taxes on certain "new" financial products and services, and is
looking at taxing real estate holdings, both rural and urban.
--Cutbacks on tax exemptions will be gradual and will first
target high-income earners.
--Greek Productivity Centre (ELKEPA) gets action plan for
Eastern Europe and North Africa in effort to develop
international cooperation.
--Xiosbank drops rates on loans. Basic business credit rate
drops by 0.50 percent to 19.75 percent.
IMERISIA
--Fears of a reversal of economic targets. Economic team
examines a series of measures which will reduce inflationary
pressures and assist in the effort to keep the cost of living
index close to 8.0 percent by year's end.
--EU report on drachma expresses fears that it has reached the
limits of its tolerance and reservations over the government's
currency policies, saying they have exhausted their
effectiveness.
KERDOS
--Workers' privileges at state utilities and organisations
(DEKO) under the spotlight. Government aims at full or partial
cutback of privileges to railways organisations (OSE),
electricity company (DEH) and telecommunications organisation
(OTE) workers and pensioners after bill on tax exemptions and
public expenditures goes through Parliament.
--ING Baring Financial Products to issue new warrant of bank
shares. Sigma to manage issue in Greece.
--Fuels fuelling inflation again.
EXPRESS
--Reform of Olympic Airways reaches a dead end. European
Commission refuses to approve 23 billion drachma second share
capital increase. Disagreement between Brussels and Athens over
government subsidies to ailing national carrier.
--"We must forget the notion of political cost and take
decisions independent of pressure from powerful groups,"
Prime Minister Costas Simitis stresses to his deputies.
--Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas
Laliotis to attempt to mend bridges with Metro construction
company "Olympic Metro" today.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Bank of Greece expects fall in interbank interest rate,
following increase in foreign exchange inflows over the past few
days. Sources say they expect a fall in the overnight rate of
between 80-90 basis points.
--Capital Market Commission proceeding with a number of
decisions and a draft bill on the modernisation of the
institutional framework and the introduction of new
financial products.
